CausalChain: Fasting/Nutrient stress -> Increased adipose lipolysis -> Elevated free fatty acids in circulation -> Hepatic activation of PPARα (promoting FGF21 and fatty acid oxidation) and PPARβ/δ (enhancing lipogenesis and PC (18:0/18:1) synthesis) -> Augmented secretion of FGF21 and PC (18:0/18:1) -> Circulation of these mediators to skeletal muscle -> PPARα-dependent upregulation of muscle fatty acid uptake and oxidation -> Reduced circulating triglycerides and improved systemic insulin sensitivity
Hypothesis: Simultaneous activation of hepatic PPARα and PPARβ/δ synergistically increases the production and secretion of FGF21 and PC (18:0/18:1), which together reprogram muscle lipid metabolism through a PPARα-mediated pathway, thereby offering a novel therapeutic target for systemic metabolic disorders such as NAFLD and insulin resistance.
Abstract: In this study, we propose a novel mechanism by which coordinated activation of hepatic PPARα and PPARβ/δ modulates the liver secretome to exert systemic metabolic benefits. Our hypothesis posits that dual activation of these pathways enhances the synthesis and release of both FGF21 and a specific phosphatidylcholine species, PC (18:0/18:1), which together act on muscle tissue via a PPARα‐dependent mechanism, thereby boosting fatty acid uptake and oxidation. This integrated signaling axis may serve as a therapeutic target for ameliorating systemic dyslipidemia, non-alcoholic fatty liver disease, and insulin resistance.
